analysis.title: Marketcolour + Global 2027 Outlooks / Nvidia / Siemens / Richemont / Hermes / Wise
key_insights: US equities closed broadly lower: SPX -35bps to 7592 (10 of 11 sectors down, Consumer Disc -177bps, Energy +188bps), NDX -30bps to 28289, RTY -166bps to 2799, VIX +6.9% to 15.86.

Commodity equities saw demand: GS Oil basket +1.30%, Natural Gas basket +0.36%. In Europe, EU Defense (-2.4%) and EU Miners (-2%) underperformed as gold fell below $4,000/oz for the first time in months (XAU -2.7% at $3880).

GS Global Macro 2027: global economy grew 2.7% in 2026, in line with potential. GS expects 2.8% in 2027 as lower energy prices and strong AI capex outweigh tighter financial conditions and more neutral fiscal policy.

GS Global Equity Outlook 2027 is overweight US and Japan, neutral N Asia and EM, underweight Europe. Equities are expected to keep rising with high volatility on attractive valuations, slower positive nominal growth, and lower yields, inflation and oil. The focus is Growth balanced with selective Defensives and beneficiaries of lower bond yields.
GS sees long-duration Growth, particularly US Hyperscalers, as attractive because growth rates are slowing and these companies still have strong, if slower, earnings growth and balance sheets.

Nvidia (Buy, PT $220, 25% upside): GS expects a measured direct impact on financials and earnings power over 12-18 months given a 12-24 month backlog and a 2-3 year product roadmap in execution. The stock's multiple is expected to take a greater hit given the uncertainty.

Siemens (Buy, PT EUR308, 10% upside): management meeting takeaways are a strong start to FY27 in automation with double-digit software growth expected, strong data center growth visibility despite possible near-term order volatility and supply-chain issues, M&A discipline, and Mobility as core to the AI strategy.
Ottobock (Buy, PT cut to EUR65 from EUR75, 60% upside): core revenue/EBITDA/EPS estimates cut 0-6% for FY26/27/28e. GS wants clarity on whether reimbursement challenges are transitory or structural.

Global Transport: freight bull market continues in Q4 with air and ocean volume growth around high-single-digit percent. The US import surge looks set to taper in November, container rates are stable near historical highs, and European airlines are cutting capacity, especially short-haul.

Hermes (Sell, PT EUR1325, 5% downside): 2027 organic sales growth trimmed to 6.1% from 7%, operating margin 40.3% vs 40.7% prior. Shares trade on 27x 2027 PE with sales growth near the sector average, so GS sees no upside. Q4 2026 sales growth expected around 4.4% y/y, in line with Q3.

Richemont: Jewellery Maisons grew +14% at constant FX in Q2 vs consensus 15.3% (buyside bar about 16%). The JM EBIT margin of 33.4% ex one-off is well ahead of consensus, implying over 100bps above expectations. The desk sees margins as a possible next leg higher but unsure they offset slower topline given positioning.

Wise: results broadly in line with Street expectations, and the Belgium overhang was removed with no admission of wrongdoing and an undisclosed, immaterial settlement. US licensing remediation is complete with an update expected in 2027, and the US platform is launching quietly with two large banks. The desk expects the stock to rise.

Siemens: near-term data center order volatility and supply-chain dynamics.
Ottobock: reimbursement challenges that may be structural rather than transitory.
Freight: the US import surge looks set to taper in November.
Richemont: slower topline growth combined with crowded positioning may limit the upside from margins.
2027 outlook: tighter financial conditions and high equity volatility.

Richemont: the desk flags positioning as a constraint on how the stock reacts to the margin beat given slower topline growth.
